data.one_liner: Lightweight spritesheet animation widget for Flutter with grid and JSON atlas support.
data.what_it_does: Renders grid-based and JSON atlas spritesheet animations with support for named frame tags, playback modes, and an external controller. It avoids widget rebuilds by utilizing a CustomPainter and handles optimization through precaching.
use_when: You need to render 2D sprite animations or pixel art in your Flutter app or game.
You are using TexturePacker or Aseprite JSON exports for sprite atlases.
You require fine-grained playback control via an external controller.
avoid_when: You need a full-fledged 2D game engine with physics and scene graphs.
You are animating vector graphics instead of raster spritesheets.
strengths: Zero widget rebuilds during playback by using CustomPainter
Supports both uniform grid and JSON atlas (TexturePacker, Aseprite) formats
weaknesses: Limited to sprite sheet animation rendering rather than full game development
Requires manual asset management and precaching for optimal loading performance

alternatives.name: rive
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose Rive if you need interactive, vector-based vector animations with a visual state machine rather than raster spritesheets.

alternatives.name: lottie
alternatives.why_pick_it: Choose Lottie if you want to render After Effects animations exported as JSON instead of frame-based sprite sheets.

data.minimal_example:
SpriteAnimation.grid(
  image: AssetImage('assets/explosion.png'),
  columns: 8,
  rows: 4,
  fps: 24,
  width: 128,
  height: 128,
)
